font-size: 15px;\"\u003EIncreased vascular permeability in acute pancreatitis causes the loss of intravenous fluid and reduces plasma volume. In severe cases, in patients with massive ascites, pleural effusion, and retroperitoneal and mesenteric edema, circulating plasma volume decreases markedly. Hypovolemia may lead to shock and acute renal failure, and, because hypovolemic shock may impair the pancreatic microcirculation and promote pancreatic ischemia and necrosis, restoration and maintenance of plasma volume is crucial in severe acute pancreatitis.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"caret-color: rgb(117, 117, 117); These include:\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EPrimary pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and secondary pulmonary hypertension (PH) as seen in chronic-obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or pulmonary fibrosis)\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ECongenital heart disease (pulmonic stenosis, right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, or a systemic RV).\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003EThe following conditions result in volume overload causing RVF:\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EValvular insufficiency (tricuspid or pulmonic)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ECongenital heart disease with a shunt (atrial septal defect (ASD) or anomalous pulmonary venous return (APVR)).\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003EAnother important mechanism that leads to RVF is intrinsic RV myocardial disease. This includes:\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ERV ischemia or infarct\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EInfiltrative diseases such as amyloidosis or sarcoidosis\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EArrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia (ARVD)\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ECardiomyopathy\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EMicrovascular disease.\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003ELastly, RVF may be caused by impaired filling which is seen in the following conditions:\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EConstrictive pericarditis\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ETricuspid stenosis\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ESystemic vasodilatory shock\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ECardiac tamponade\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003ESuperior vena cava syndrome\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003EHypovolemia.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-weight: bolder;\"\u003EB) What are the pharmacological and non pharmacological interventions used in the management of this patient and what are the efficacy of each one of them?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cp\u003E)Pharmacological interventions\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E(meta analysis with each class of drugs)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPreload reducers\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDiuretics\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAfterload reducers-ace inhibitors\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERate controlling agents-beta blockers\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAntiepileptics for known case of epilepsy\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EInsulin for glycemic control in diabetes.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENon pharmacological interventions\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESalt and fluid restriction\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"BlinkMacSystemFont, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Fira Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Droid Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, sans-serif\"\u003EIndividualized salt and fluid restriction can improve signs and symptoms of CHF with no negative effects on thirst, appetite, or QoL in patients with moderate to severe CHF and previous signs of fluid retention.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-weight: bolder;
